name: Thistle
desc: A dried teasel standing hero-scale against the wind — a fluted, hard-hatched stalk carrying spine-toothed cauline leaves up to an ovoid capitulum whose imbricated bracts sit on a golden-angle spiral, the whole architecture leaning and recovering on a wind that never repeats while pappus florets tear loose from the crown and ride away.

energy.doc: how hard the wind bends the plant, how the leaves flutter, how fast it sheds

scale.doc: hero height vs min(width,height) — 1 stands 0.48 tall, 2.2 towers out of frame

density.doc: cauline leaf pairs + bract count on the head + seated pappus

hue.doc: dry-tissue hue (the engraving keeps its key light near it)

x.doc: where the plant is rooted across the frame

y.doc: where the plant is rooted down the frame — it grows upward from here

head.doc: capitulum proportion — a lean spike at 0, a fat drum-head teasel at 1

pose.doc: standing = erect, idling on the wind; bowed = the head's weight arcs the stalk over; seeding = the crown pours pappus away; thrash = storm-whipped, the whip landing on the beat

style.doc: aesthetic — white-line engraving (dark mass, form built purely from pale hatching + a rim light, reads on any ground); Atkins photogram, pale mass on nothing; additive translucent radiograph of the head's interior; flat unlit mass, no interior at all

seed.doc: seeds the pappus release order, drift and spin

alpha.doc: opacity over whatever is behind it
